known_final_diagnosis: Analysis of pleural fluid showed elevated triglycerides of 319 mg/dL consistent with chylothorax. Flow cytometry of the pleural fluid showed that 3% of total cells were monotypic B cells, expressing CD19, CD20, CD45 and kappa light chain but were negative for CD5 and CD10. Cytology of fluid revealed moderately cellular effusion with abundant small lymphocytes mixed with a few reactive mesothelial cells. Findings were consistent with B-cell lymphoma.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 50-year-old woman with known Waldenstrom's macroglobulinaemia (WM, low-grade B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma) diagnosed 3 years prior and asymptomatic on observation presented with acute right-sided pleuritic chest pain (1 day duration) and progressive dyspnoea (1 month duration). Physical examination revealed palpable adenopathy in bilateral anterior cervical and left supraclavicular regions with absent breath sounds in the right lower lobe. Chest imaging demonstrated a large right pleural effusion with compressive atelectasis and mediastinal shift, along with increased adenopathy in the lower neck and upper thorax compared to imaging from 3 years prior, including lymphadenopathy at the thoracic duct near the confluence of the left subclavian and left internal jugular veins. Thoracentesis yielded 1.4 L of milky fluid with elevated triglycerides (319 mg/dL) consistent with chylothorax. Pleural fluid analysis showed monotypic B cells (3% of total cells) expressing CD19, CD20, CD45, and kappa light chain but negative for CD5 and CD10, with abundant small lymphocytes on cytology. Repeat bone marrow biopsy performed 1 month later demonstrated disease progression with 90% infiltrate of small-to-intermediate lymphocytes and plasma cells, with B-cell phenotype (CD19+, CD20+, CD23+, surface immunoglobulin kappa). The patient was initiated on ibrutinib 420 mg nightly, and the pleural effusion resolved within 2 months without need for further thoracentesis.
